caption:
The Pantheon's dome is pure unreinforced concrete, and after 2,000 years nobody has ever built a bigger one — and there's an entire second country hiding inside Rome's city limits. 👀

Comment your guess for which fact surprised you most before you swipe ⬇️

1. The Pantheon
The Pantheon is made of pure unreinforced concrete — no steel, no support — and after almost two millennia, nobody has built a bigger dome. Modern engineers still study how the Romans did it.

2. The Colosseum
For its opening games in 80 AD, the arena was filled with water and scaled-down warships fought inside it. The underneath tunnels you see today are the reason the sea battles ended, as they made the flooding impossible.

3. Trevi Fountain
Tourists toss in roughly €1.3 million a year to the Trevi Fountain. Every night, workers collect the coins — and all of it goes to charity.

4. Vatican City
Vatican City is the smallest independent state on Earth (0.44 km²) and it sits right in the middle of Rome. You can be walking down a Roman street and simply cross into another country without realizing it.

5. Passetto del Borgo
The Passetto del Borgo is a hidden elevated passage connecting the Vatican to Castel Sant'Angelo. In 1527, a pope literally ran for his life through it while Rome was being sacked around him.

6. Palatine Hill
Roman emperors built their residences on Palatine Hill — "palatium" in Latin. Every palace in every language is, without knowing it, named after this one spot in Rome.

7. The Roman Forum
Centuries of rebuilding mean today's streets sit meters above the ancient ones. Basilicas, houses, and entire streets lie buried beneath the modern city — many still unexcavated.
